prompt:
EDIT the reference image(s). Keep this exact design identity — the silhouette language, colours, materials, lighting and 1-px near-black navy outline of:
Retro 16-bit video game explosion sprite sheet in SNES-era pixel art inspired style, on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background: exactly twelve frames laid out as three rows with exactly four frames in each row, evenly spaced on a regular grid with even green gutters, each frame centered in its own cell, read left to right and top to bottom as one blast played forward, the blast growing and then fading from frame to frame.
Top row, frames one to four: frame one a tiny tight spark of white-hot lemon light with four short radial spike lines; frame two a small bright pale-gold sphere with a crisp dark outline and short spikes; frame three the fireball doubled in size, a hot cream core wrapped in rolling outlined petals of amber flame; frame four larger again, tangerine flame lobes curling outward and the first dark smoke puffs crowning the top.
Middle row, frames five to eight: the fireball at full size with a cream core and orange petals throwing short spark arms to the sides; then the core cooling to burnt orange; then the flame lobes shredding into separate rust-red and brown-grey smoke clouds that still keep a round shape; then smoke dominating with ember sparks streaming outward on straight lines.
Bottom row, frames nine to twelve: a wide slow cloud of dark ember-grey smoke veined with the last dim red cracks of inner light; the cloud breaking into separate hard-edged puffs; a few thinning puffs with lone orange embers drifting clear; finally just two or three faint grey wisps and one gold point-spark.
Palette strictly the explosion ramp: white-hot cream to lemon gold to amber to rust orange to deep ember red over smoke grey. Bold dark outlines on every flame lobe and smoke puff, flat saturated fills with three-step shading lit from the top left, hard pixel edges, no soft glow halo onto the background, no shadows, no cell borders, no grid lines, no text, no labels, no numbers.

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.- Every subject sits well inside the sheet: at least 48 px of unbroken flat #51e018 key between every subject and the nearest sheet border, and all four sheet corners are pure #51e018.
- SIXTEEN (16) equal square cells in a 4×4 grid, reading order: one continuous 16-frame explosion progression of the referenced fireball design — ignition, white-hot bloom, full ball, ring of burning debris, breakdown, embers, smoke decay across the sixteen cells in strictly even steps. One shared center anchor, equal cells, nothing else. Exactly SIXTEEN cells.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 1040×1040 px. Produce EXACTLY 16 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: retro 16-bit pixel art, chunky visible square pixels, flat saturated fills with a three-step shading ramp lit from the top-left, crisp 1-px near-black navy outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no soft gradients on the background, no motion blur.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, fire explosion stock photo, mushroom cloud, cartoon smiley, text, numbers, arrows, cell borders, frames merging, different explosions each frame, green tint on the smoke, soft glow halo, watermark, blurry
